CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Add SecurityContext to all Job and CronJob pod specs

# GitHub Issue #128: Add SecurityContext to all Job and CronJob pod specs

**Category**: security | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: The db_sync Job, bootstrap Job, and fernet/credential rotation CronJobs in reconcile_database.go, reconcile_bootstrap.go, reconcile_fernet.go, and reconcile_credential.go do not set any SecurityContext. Add runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and seccompProfile type RuntimeDefault to all Job and CronJob pod templates, matching the security posture already applied to the Deployment pods.

**Motivation**: Clusters enforcing Pod Security Standards (Restricted profile) will reject these pods outright. This is a hard blocker for production deployments in security-conscious environments.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_database.go`
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_bootstrap.go`
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_fernet.go`
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_credential.go`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] All Job and CronJob pod specs include securityContext with runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and seccompProfile RuntimeDefault
- [ ] Pods pass Pod Security Restricted admission
- [ ] Existing E2E tests continue to pass with the new security context

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/128

<commit-best-practices>
<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0045): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>

<git-identity>
  <rule name="author">ALWAYS use --author flag: git commit --author "Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>" -m "..."</rule>
  <rule name="co-authored-by">Do NOT add any Co-Authored-By trailer. Never add "Co-Authored-By: Claude" or similar.</rule>
  <rule name="trailers">Append these trailers at the end of the commit message body, separated by a blank line:
    AI-assisted: Claude Code
    On-behalf-of: @SAP christian.berendt@sap.com
    Signed-off-by: Christian Berendt <berendt@23technologies.cloud>
  </rule>
</git-identity>
